value.note: verbatim: ““ Commitment ”: as to any Lender, the obligation of such Lender, if any, to make Loans and participate in Letters of Credit in an aggregate principal and/or face amount not to exceed the amount set forth under the heading “Commitment” opposite such Lender’s name on Schedule 1.1A or in the Assignment and Assumption pursuant to which such Lender became a party hereto, as the same may be changed from time to time pursuant to the terms hereof. As of the Closing Date, the amount of the Total Commitments is $1,000,000,000.”

value.value: Term Benchmark Loans: Adjusted Term SOFR + Applicable Margin; RFR Loans: Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR + Applicable Margin; ABR Loans: ABR + Applicable Margin. Applicable Margin for Term Benchmark/RFR Loans ranges 1.125%-1.75% and for ABR Loans 0.125%-0.75% (per leverage/ratings grids). Adjusted Term SOFR = Term SOFR Rate + 0.10%; Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR = Daily Simple SOFR + 0.10%. Floor = zero.
value.note: verbatim: “(a) (i) Each Term Benchmark Loan shall bear interest for each day during each Interest Period with respect thereto at a rate per annum equal to the Adjusted Term SOFR determined for such day plus the Applicable Margin and (ii) each RFR Loan ... shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR plus the Applicable Margin. (b) Each ABR Loan shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the ABR plus the Applicable Margin.”

value.value: Termination Date = fifth anniversary of the Closing Date (Closing Date: March 26, 2024), subject to extension per Section 2.18; Borrower shall repay all outstanding Loans on the Termination Date
value.note: verbatim: ““ Termination Date ”: the fifth anniversary of the Closing Date, subject to the extension thereof pursuant to Section 2.18 .”

value.value: Consolidated Leverage Ratio not to exceed 4.00 to 1.00 (or 4.50 to 1.00 during any Acquisition Step-Up Period), tested at end of each fiscal quarter for the four-consecutive-fiscal-quarter period on a Pro Forma Basis
value.note: verbatim: “7.1 Financial Condition Covenant . Permit the Consolidated Leverage Ratio, calculated as at the end of any fiscal quarter for the period of four consecutive fiscal quarters of the Borrower then ended, on a Pro Forma Basis, to exceed (x) 4.00 to 1.00, or (y) 4.50 to 1.00 for any fiscal quarter during any Acquisition Step-Up Period, calculated as at the end of any fiscal quarter ending during any Acquisition Step-Up Period; provided that that there shall be no more than two Acquisition Step-Up Periods after the Closing Date and each Acquisition Step-Up Period shall be separated by at least two calendar quarters.”

value.value: Facility is unsecured by its terms (no security package granted at closing). Springing guarantee: each Domestic Subsidiary that guarantees Borrower Indebtedness (clauses (a)/(c)) of $150,000,000 or more must guarantee the Obligations within 60 days (Section 6.7). Equal-and-ratable lien covenant under Section 7.3 (secure Obligations equally and ratably if Liens securing Indebtedness are created).
value.note: verbatim: “6.7 Subsidiary Guarantee . (a) Each Domestic Subsidiary that guarantees Indebtedness of the Borrower of the type contemplated by clauses (a) and (c) of the definition thereof in an aggregate principal amount of $150,000,000 or more will guarantee the Obligations under the Facility pursuant to documentation reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent within 60 days of the incurrence of such guarantee (or such longer period as may be agreed by the Administrative Agent).”

value.value: Events of Default (Section 8.1): (a) payment defaults (principal when due; interest/other within 5 days); (b) breach of representations/warranties in material respect; (c) default under Section 6.4(a)(i)/(ii), 6.6(a) or Section 7; (d) default of other covenants, 30-day cure after notice; (e) cross-default/cross-acceleration on Indebtedness exceeding $200,000,000 in aggregate; (f) bankruptcy/insolvency (60-day period for involuntary); (g) ERISA events with Material Adverse Effect; (h) judgments of $200,000,000 or more unstayed 60 days; (i) change of control (>50% of outstanding common stock). Automatic acceleration on Borrower bankruptcy (clause (f)(i)/(ii)); otherwise acceleration/termination on Required Lenders' direction. Cash collateral posting for undrawn Letters of Credit upon acceleration. No scheduled mandatory prepayment; Section 2.5 provides optional prepayments without premium/penalty. L/C denominated-in-foreign-currency overage cash-collateral requirement (Section 3.1).
value.note: verbatim: “8.1 Events of Default . synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — a non-cash impairment and intact franchise economics collide with a genuine, consensus-confirmed revenue/CV deceleration.

bull_points.claim: The de-rate was driven by a discrete Feb-2026 gap-down carrying a $150M Digital goodwill impairment — a non-cash one-off charge, not a demonstrated cash-earnings collapse.

Absolute EBITDA has held and risen through the de-rate — $1,309M (FY24) → $1,311M (FY25) → $1,337M (LTM Mar-2026) — even as the margin % drifted from 21% to 20%, so the optical margin softness masks flat-to-rising dollar profit.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: The core Insights subscription model (78% of revenue) continues to show engagement gains — overall monthly-active-user engagement up over 170bps YoY in Q1-2026 — the retention driver management ties to renewal.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Contract value, the leading indicator of subscription revenue, grew 1% YoY in Q1-2026 and 3.5% ex-US-federal, isolating the drag to the federal book rather than the core franchise.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Return on capital remains high and stable through the de-rate — RoCE 18.2% (FY24) → 18.6% (FY25) → 19.4% (LTM) — consistent with a durable franchise, not a business in structural decay.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Ratios (Return on Capital %, multi-year columns)

bull_points.claim: The company is aggressively retiring equity — share count -13.1% over ~1.8 years, with $535M bought back in Q1-2026 alone — reducing the share base into the drawdown.
Leverage is modest with strong coverage — net-debt/EBITDA 1.3x and EBITDA/interest 10.1x — far inside the 4.00x covenant leverage ceiling, giving balance-sheet room the terminal thesis would deny.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense [LTM 12 months Mar-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: The name self-funds: latest-quarter OCF positive and LTM FCF positive at $1,064.2M, so runway and buyback capacity rest on generated cash, not new debt.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Cash Flow 'Levered Free Cash Flow' [LTM 12 months Mar-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: Guidance delivery has been reliable — EPS-Normalized met/beat guided floor 28/30 and EBITDA 42/46 resolved, with the most recent FY2025 marks MET.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Guidance (latest guide + sign-aware delivery track-record)

bear_points.claim: Revenue growth has stalled to a stop — FY25 +4% decelerating to LTM, with Q1-2026 revenue -1.5% YoY, the first same-quarter contraction in the series, indicating the top line is no longer compounding.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement + Segments + Ratios (multi-year columns)

bear_points.claim: This is a REAL signal, not an optical one: forward consensus confirms the deceleration rather than reverting it — FY26 revenue estimate cut from $7,011.9M (12m ago) to $6,431.2M (latest), a -8% path, and EBITDA -7%, so the cheap forward multiple sits on a still-falling numerator.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

bear_points.claim: Contract value growth of only 1% YoY (3.5% ex-federal) is weak for a subscription franchise historically compounding double digits, and management attributes further slowing to client decision deferral in March 2026 — a demand-side, not one-off, drag.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

bear_points.claim: Near-term forward revisions are overwhelmingly negative — Revenue FQ2/FQ3 2026 breadth 0 up / 11 down over 2-3 months — a broad-based downgrade, not one stray broker.

The stock's collapse is idiosyncratic and severe — down ~45% over 180d while the mid-cap benchmark rose ~12% (a ~57pt relative loss) — the market is pricing a company-specific problem, not a sector sell-off.

decisive_question.question: Is the contract-value deceleration a transient, federal-and-macro-driven pause in an intact subscription compounder (overshoot), or the leading edge of a structural demand impairment in the core Insights franchise (value trap)?

evidence_for.claim: CV grew 1% YoY but 3.5% ex-US-federal with GTS/GBS wallet retention of 97-99%, and management flagged the March slowing as geopolitical decision-deferral, framing it as cyclical.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: Engagement — the stated retention driver — improved over 170bps YoY, and RoCE held at 19.4% LTM, consistent with a franchise whose economics are intact.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Ratios (Return on Capital %, multi-year columns)

evidence_against.claim: Forward consensus revenue has been cut -8% over 12 months to $6,431.2M and Q1-2026 already printed -1.5% YoY, so the deceleration is showing in reported results and estimates, not just tone.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

evidence_against.claim: Near-term revenue revision breadth is 0 up / 11 down across FQ2 and FQ3 2026, a broad analyst downgrade that argues against a quick snap-back.

key_unknowns: Company-adjusted LTM EBITDA and adjusted EPS are not in the revised guidance, so the adjusted forward EV/EBITDA and adjusted leverage cannot be computed — the multiple debate rests on a trailing-only basis.

No segment-level EBITDA breakout is disclosed, so it is impossible to isolate whether the Insights subscription core is holding margin while lower-margin segments drag — an opaque gap that obscures the quality of the profit mix.

The peer set is flagged HETEROGENEOUS (market caps $751M–$119.1B, 159x span); every peer multiple and the 'cheap vs median' framing is a confidence-gated input, not a clean benchmark, and the discount cannot be cleanly split into earned vs residual from the supplied deltas.
Whether the CV deceleration stabilizes or worsens beyond the US-federal drag through FQ2/FQ3 2026 is the crux and is not resolvable from the data on file.
Covenant basis leverage and the ≤12m maturity wall are UNKNOWN/not disclosed; the filing states no near-term maturity but the covenant-basis EBITDA is not provided.
The revised-guidance 99.1 exhibit for the Feb-2026 gap-down was not parsed, so the magnitude of any forward-outlook cut delivered with the impairment is not captured.

business_description.value: Gartner, Inc. provides business and technology insights for decisions and performance on an organization’s mission-critical priorities in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and internationally. It operates through three segments: Insights, Conferences, and Consulting. The Research segment delivers insights through subscription services, such as access to published content, data and benchmarks, and direct access to a network of business and technology experts. The Conferences segment offers executives and teams in an organization the opportunity to learn, share, and network through its Symposium/Xpo series and peer-driven sessions, as well as conferences focused on specific business roles and topics. The Consulting segment provides technology-driven strategic initiatives, including custom analysis and on-the-ground support to senior executives. This segment also offers actionable solutions for IT-related priorities, including IT cost optimization, digital transformation, and IT sourcing optimization. Gartner, Inc. was founded in 1979 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.
